assessments.conclusion: The complete frozen patch modifies only the two regular files named in the allowlist. It is read by Git apply, never evaluated as shell/Python/Rust. Git commands use argument arrays. No repository script, product entry point, build or validator is invoked. Exact before blobs and patch SHA-256 precede apply; the staged path set is checked afterward. No applicable .gitattributes or root modules shadowing the explicitly imported Python modules were found in the frozen base.

The source checks exactly two distinct allowed target paths, the literal repository, task/round, checked-out event SHA, sole declared parent, exactly three added carrier paths, each old blob, patch digest, resulting path set, and both resulting byte counts/Git blob IDs. Both captured byte arrays enter verified_objects before any POST. The frozen manifest is part of the reviewed authority; this verdict does not authorize arbitrary later manifest/workflow revisions.

The job requests contents:write and passes github.token through GH_TOKEN to the materialization step. The only application network write is POST to the literal HTTPS endpoint https://api.github.com/repos/bhrumom/fabushi-desktop/git/blobs. The redirect handler refuses redirected requests. Source diagnostics and the uploaded receipt contain paths, hashes, counts and revision identities, not the token or Authorization header. No API path, host, shell command or artifact path is derived from patch content. Checkout and artifact actions retain the established v4 dependencies.

Requests have a 60-second timeout and response context managers; the job has a 10-minute timeout. Upload responses must match the expected Git blob IDs. The receipt is written only after both uploads pass. If the second upload fails, the first may remain as an unreferenced immutable blob, but the job has no commit/tree/ref update and emits no successful receipt. There is no broad cleanup or process-lifetime manipulation.

For the intended single-commit push from the exact base to the carrier on the named branch, the three changed paths select the carrier and do not match the source-authority/runtime push path filters. Other inspected push branch filters exclude this branch. This is not a claim about unrelated dispatches or a cumulative PR diff. The receipt explicitly records product_validation_executed_by_staging_job=false; no product-validation credit follows from carrier success.

The declared root API consumer waits for the exact successful carrier job and receipt plus both remote objects, applies 22 pinned object entries and three sha:null removals to carrier tree 711a04b643e3df2746dbe02c856030d359dcea5a, and rejects any returned tree except 9e40308b710fcc66602623880857512a20a5331a before creating a product commit. It requires the actual carrier as sole parent, a fresh lease and expected_sha=432eb4fc9eb64967aa4430b82787e8df80d67afa with force=false, followed by remote commit/tree/parent/content readback and carrier absence. These are necessary consumer conditions, not steps enforced or performed by the carrier job. The declared arguments agree with the frozen tree difference.

The job checks after_bytes and after_blob, but does not evaluate the manifest's after_sha256 fields. Those fields were independently matched to the frozen target objects in this review. The exact patch digest and expected Git object checks satisfy the existing carrier contract; this is not a claim of an additional runtime SHA-256 check.
Carrier Actions execution, final API publication, post-publication readback and product source/runtime evidence remain pending and are not approved as completed by this verdict.
